question: A can do a work in 17 days and B can do the same work in 19 days. If they work on it together for 6 days, then what fraction of the work is left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined 1-day work = (17 + 19) ÷ (17 × 19) = 36/323

Work completed in 6 days = 6 × (36/323) = 216/323

Fraction of work remaining = 1 − 216/323 = 107/323

**∴ The correct answer is 107/323.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 17 days

Time taken by B = 19 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 19 + 17 = 36 units/day

⇒ Work done by A and B together in 6 days = 36 × 6 = 216 units

⇒ Remaining work = 323 − 216 = 107 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 107/323

**∴ The correct answer is 107/323.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

If a pipe fills a tank in X hours and another empties it in Y hours, their combined net rate is (1/X − 1/Y). The time taken to fill the tank is XY ÷ (Y − X) if Y > X.

Alternate Days Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people). Find how many full cycles fit into the total work before calculating the remainder.
